import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

output_path = "/mnt/data/outputs/347-49_0_243f036f/1_347-49_output.xlsx"

# Ensure we have exactly 384 rows and 4 columns as stated; if shorter/longer, adjust by padding/truncating
target_rows = 384
target_cols = 4
# If fewer rows, append NaN rows; if more, truncate

    extra = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=range(target_rows - df.shape[0]), columns=df.columns)
    df = pd.concat([df, extra], ignore_index=True)
elif df.shape[0] > target_rows:
    df = df.iloc[:target_rows].reset_index(drop=True)

# Identify indices where Column D (3) exactly equals the string "Gross Pay"
# Use string comparison safely even if cells are NaN
gross_indices = df.index[df[3].astype(str) == "Gross Pay"].tolist()

# Collect row indices that are entirely blank (all A-D are NaN) and are immediately above each Gross Pay row.
rows_to_drop = set()
for idx in gross_indices:
    j = idx - 1

        for c in range(target_cols):
